title: Rolemap
short_description: Maps your skills to live job-market demand. 1st place, ACM UTD semester projects.
description:
An ACM UTD semester project: a platform that maps a user's skills against live job-market demand and tells them where they stand.

I led a team of four and architected the full-stack application and its backend microservices — my first real backend work, learned from scratch on this project. That includes 5+ API microservices that parse resumes and integrate Knowledge Graphs while holding sub-50 ms latency SLAs, and a web-scraping backend pulling 10,000+ live job-market records through secure REST endpoints.

Presented the build and demo to 200+ industry professionals and judges. Placed 1st at ACM UTD.

title: Kids-U Donor & Volunteer Database
short_description: 24-table PostgreSQL/Prisma backend for a local nonprofit's volunteer, grant and donor operations.
description:
Kids-U, a Dallas nonprofit, needed a backend system to run its volunteer, grant and donor operations. Built through EPICS (Engineering Projects in Community Service) by a six-person student team working directly with the nonprofit's stakeholders.

I was project lead: owned the backend schema design, managed milestones, delegated work across the team, and handled communication with the client to turn operational needs into technical requirements.

The result is a 24-table PostgreSQL + Prisma architecture supporting 50,000+ records with ACID guarantees. Query-performance work cut frontend data-fetching time by 60% (2.5 s → under 1 s).

title: Hypershift
short_description: Stock-movement prediction with temporal hyperbolic hypergraph neural networks.
description:
Built around the ideas in THINK: Temporal Hypergraph Hyperbolic Network (Agarwal et al., ICDM 2022): model the market as a time-evolving hypergraph embedded in hyperbolic (Poincaré-ball) space, so higher-order relationships between stocks that pairwise graphs miss become visible.

I modeled stock movement as temporal hyperbolic hypergraphs and used distance-aware, attention-based aggregation to weigh relationships between nodes.

Result: a 10% improvement over the baselines the reference paper benchmarks against (GConvGRU, EGCN, DCRNN, TGCN, STHGCN).

title: Dattack
short_description: Autonomous multi-agent AI data consultant. Best Overall Project, ACM Education hackathon (50+ teams).
description:
Dattack is an autonomous AI "data consultant": hand it a dataset and it decides what to investigate, runs the analysis, and writes up business-ready findings.

I architected the multi-agent system in LangGraph to generate statistically rigorous investigation DAGs, backed by a deterministic "Curiosity Pipeline" of 20 Python scripts that mathematically profile a dataset (outlier detection, variance analysis). A separate Critic agent enforces that every claim is provable from the data before it reaches the report.

On the frontend I built an interactive SPA with a custom HTML Canvas renderer that draws the live investigation DAG — 1,000+ nodes without frame drops — fed by an SSE + FastAPI streaming architecture delivering updates at under 200 ms latency.

Won Best Overall Project at ACM Education against 50+ teams; judges cited it as a reference for analyst reporting efficiency.

title: Comet Navigator
short_description: AI-powered student planner for UTD. Figma Track Winner, HackAI 2026.
description:
UTD students juggle eLearning for assignments, Outlook for announcements, club sites for events, personal calendars, and group chats for study sessions. Comet Navigator pulls that into one place and plans the day for you.

Team of four (with Ethan Collins, Anirudh Devatha and Atharva Mishra). I owned the Figma design and the frontend build, plus the two most technically distinct pieces: the Gemini-driven recommendation logic and the authentication system. The recommender weighs availability, productivity, commitments, interests and location to suggest study blocks, campus events, study partners and an optimized daily schedule. I also helped integrate university data through the Nebula API — open study rooms, auto-assigned rooms for sessions, and clubs filtered by interest, major and past involvement.

Shipped: interactive dashboard, dynamic calendar, study-room finder, club discovery, buddy matching, study-session queue, onboarding survey, and an end-of-day feedback swipe UI.

Hardest part was the Nebula scraper — content only loaded on scroll and the markup was a maze, so the right selectors took real trial and error. The recommender also needed tuning before its class-time and club suggestions stopped being noise.

Won the Figma Track (Best Use of Figma) at HackAI 2026.

title: ASA DataFest 2026
short_description: 7M+ rows of hospital data, 48 hours, one recommendation: where to put the next hospital.
description:
ASA DataFest is a 48-hour national competition. The 2026 prompt: analyze hospital data to guide hospital-placement decisions.

I led a team of five through 7M+ rows (7 GB+) of data in R. We fit SuperLearner ensemble models and ran Monte Carlo simulations to probabilistically evaluate 100+ candidate sites, trading off cost, speed and accuracy, then presented economically optimal placement recommendations to industry judges.

title: Lock In Labs
short_description: Multi-agent LLM planner with real-time computer-vision focus tracking. Best Productivity App, HackMars 1.0.
description:
A productivity app that turns a goal into a plan and then watches whether you actually stick to it.

I engineered the multi-agent LLM backend that generates task DAGs under strict JSON schemas — the schema enforcement eliminated cycle-generation errors entirely. Alongside it I integrated a real-time YOLOv11 computer-vision microservice that processes video at 30+ FPS with under 50 ms inference latency to monitor the user's state.

Won Best Productivity App (Productivity Track) at HackMars 1.0.

title: RateMyCareer
short_description: Zero-data-loss ETL pipeline over 250K+ Reddit posts a week, serving career-classification models.
description:
A career-advice tool built on scraped Reddit data.

I built the fault-tolerant ETL pipeline that ingests, normalizes and processes 250K+ real-time text records a week with zero data loss, and the API microservices that serve the classification models — 500+ frontend requests per minute at under 100 ms latency.

title: Slither.io RL Agent
short_description: PPO agent trained to a 20:1 kill/death ratio in Slither.io.
description:
A self-directed project: train an autonomous agent to play Slither.io competitively.

Two fixes made it work. Sparse rewards were stalling training, so I pre-trained the agent on human gameplay with behavior cloning before fine-tuning with PPO. And instead of feeding raw pixels to a CNN, I designed a custom "Radar" vector observation space, which sped up convergence dramatically.

The agent reached a 20:1 kill/death ratio.

title: Instagranime
short_description: Instagram-style anime recommender with O(1) online preference updates.
description:
A personal project: an Instagram-style feed for discovering anime, where every swipe updates your recommendations instantly.

The Flask backend does online learning — user-preference-vector updates run in O(1) — and held up under 1,000+ concurrent users. Behind it, a concurrent Scrapy service with 5+ distributed spiders harvested and normalized 10,000+ records in under two hours.

title: The CINEX Film Club
short_description: President for two years. 50+ members, 30+ students trained, 2,000+ Facebook followers.
description: Ran the club for two years. Grew membership to 50+ and personally trained 30+ students in filmmaking, while building the club's Facebook presence to 2,000+ followers and 1,700+ likes.

title: Generous Souls United
short_description: Founded and led a student service organization. 250+ gifts and meals distributed.
description: Founded Generous Souls United, a student service organization, and led it for three years. We ran education programs for underprivileged children and organized charity drives that distributed 250+ gifts and meals.
